title: A GPU FFT Wrapper to Co-optimize Floating-Point Precision and Library Selection via Predictive Error Modeling
problem: FFT libraries exhibit different performance-accuracy tradeoffs at different scales and precisions; selecting optimal library+precision combination requires manual exploration or expensive profiling
motivation: FFT is ubiquitous in scientific computing; enabling automatic precision/library selection could unlock substantial performance gains (>40% speedup) with guaranteed error bounds
method: The system wraps multiple GPU FFT libraries (fast algorithms for specific math operations) with a lightweight machine-learning predictor that learns to estimate result accuracy. When you run an FFT operation, it samples characteristics of your input, predicts the error that each library-precision combination would produce, then automatically selects the fastest and most energy-efficient option that still meets your accuracy threshold.
key_novelty: It's the first system to use machine learning to simultaneously select both the GPU library and floating-point precision (how many bits to use for numbers), rather than optimizing each choice separately.
contributions: Characterization of precision-performance-accuracy tradeoffs across FFT libraries
Lightweight ML predictor achieving 98% selection accuracy
Wrapper library seamlessly integrating into existing workflows
Mean speedups exceeding 40% vs double-precision baseline
limitations: Limited to FFT; error model accuracy depends on input features; overhead of sampling/prediction not quantified; applicable to GPU only
